Lorenz curve and Gini coefficient

Source: R/metrics.R
gini.Rd

How concentrated is a quantity (points, shots, assists) among the top n contributors? lorenz() returns the curve, gini() the coefficient in [0, 1]. Only the n largest values are used, because adding deep-bench players inflates inequality; compare teams with the same n. The Gini is the normalised area between the line of equality and the curve, so with n players its maximum is 1.

Usage

gini(x, n = NULL)

lorenz(x, n = NULL)

Arguments

x

Non-negative values (one per player).

n

Number of largest values to keep (NULL = all).

Examples

pts <- c(2028, 1734, 1261, 1056, 1918, 1236, 600, 400, 50)
gini(pts, n = 8)
#> [1] 0.2798369
lorenz(pts, n = 8)
#> # A tibble: 9 × 3
#>    rank people  value
#>   <int>  <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1     0  0     0     
#> 2     1  0.125 0.0391
#> 3     2  0.25  0.0977
#> 4     3  0.375 0.201 
#> 5     4  0.5   0.322 
#> 6     5  0.625 0.445 
#> 7     6  0.75  0.614 
#> 8     7  0.875 0.802 
#> 9     8  1     1
